name: Duene
prior: Audio-rate Kuramoto synthesis exists in niche/academic tools and one new effect plugin: Chiral Audio Foxfire (2025/26; 16 voices in a Kuramoto mean field as a chorus/ensemble EFFECT; Coupling knob: drift -> partial sync -> flicker at the critical point -> lock; VST3/AU/standalone; VS: kvraudio.com/product/foxfire-by-chiral-audio, rekkerd.org chiral-audio-launches-effect-plugins); Nolan Lem 'Kuroscillators' (Max/MSP objects, rhythmic and audio schemes; SMC 2019 paper; VS: github.com/nolanlem/Kuroscillators, smc2019.uma.es P3_09); 'Kuramoto drone' (browser drone, configurable oscillator count and tuning; VS: mi.wrocenter.pl/en/kuramoto-drone); Feng Ling 'Synchronized Synthesis' (MATLAB/VST, ~10^3 hydrodynamically coupled oscillators, no pitch control; VS: mathworks.com fileexchange/92588); Moon, NIME 2024, Kuramoto vs Janus for synthesis (VS: nime.org/proc/nime2024_60); Melu Freak (Eurorack, 2 phase-synchronised oscillators, not a population; VS: gearnews.com freak-phase-synchronised-dual-oscillator-eurorack). Dune physics: Douady et al. 2006 'The song of the dunes as a self-synchronized instrument' (VS: arxiv.org/pdf/nlin/0412047), Hunt & Vriend 'Booming sand dunes' (dominant 70-110 Hz plus harmonics; VS: www2.ess.ucla.edu/~jewitt/Hunt10.pdf), Andreotti wave-particle mode locking (VS: arxiv.org/pdf/1201.0958, 1305.2241), Wikipedia singing sand (mechanism still debated; VS). 'Singing Dunes' Ableton rack by Raz Mesinai is a preset, not a model (VS: ableton.com/en/blog/singing-dunes). Not found: a pitched instrument whose playable control IS the noise-to-tone phase transition of a coupled grain population. In Myzel: Koerner (grain textures), Glühwurm (sister idea, sub-audio Kuramoto).
costNotes: Worklet only (24 coupled phase oscillators with a per-sample mean field is sample-level DSP). The idea's 0.75 ('2 x 16-resonator bank') is wrong for the design as written: a resonator is 4 mul + 2 add (~5 ns/sample, R: webaudio.md section 4), while one Kuramoto grain as specified needs sin(psi - theta), cos theta and sin theta (3 table lookups ~10 ns each) plus p(theta) = ((1 - cos theta)/2)^(2 + 6 k) with a per-sample Math.pow (~30-40 ns) -> ~70 ns per oscillator-sample, x 24 = ~1.7 us/sample = 8 % of a 48 kHz core = ~13 Nebel units, x1.0-1.5 on a phone. Fixes that bring it back: (1) integrate the coupling at a sub-rate (every 16-32 samples; the mean field in the co-rotating frame drifts at ~Streuung * f, i.e. 25 Hz at f = 100 Hz, far below the 1.5-3 kHz sub-rate) -> coupling cost / 16; (2) pulse shape from a table indexed by theta with Koernung selecting among ~8 tables (no pow); (3) better: event-based impulses - per sample only 24 phase accumulators + wrap tests (~3 ns each), emit one impulse with random amplitude per wrap into a shared short 'Korn' kernel (IIR 1-2 poles) -> ~0.1-0.2 us/sample total. With (1)+(2): ~0.25 us/sample ~ 1.2 % core ~ 2 units; with (3): ~0.4-0.6 units + node 0.06 + 3 params 0.09 + native peaking 0.06. Estimate 1.1 for the (1)+(2) design, 0.6 for the event-based one, 13 for the naive one - MEASURE with research/bench before committing (the idea says so). L3 with 48 grains ~ 2x.
soundHeld: The most original gesture of the four: lift the finger slowly and hear 24 rustling grains fall into one booming tone - a phase transition under the finger, with Bebung as vibrato of the drone and setF gliding all omega_i. Caveats that decide whether it is music or a demo: (a) with Streuung 0.25 and N = 24 the order parameter R fluctuates by ~1/sqrt(N) ~ 0.2, so the 'Einrasten' is a mushy crossfade, not a snap; first-order Kuramoto has no hysteresis, so there is no moment to find - the finger just scales a continuous blend. A second-order (inertia) Kuramoto or an adaptive K gives bistability and a real click-in/click-out with hysteresis [A], which is what the pitch 'den Moment des Einrastens suchen' promises; (b) the synced state is a jittered pulse train = buzzy, supersaw-ish at mid pitches; dunes boom at 70-110 Hz with harmonics (VS: Hunt & Vriend), so the sweet range is 40-200 Hz with a body lowpass, and above ~300 Hz it is a rough Koerner; (c) the unsynced state at R ~ 0 is 24 random pulse trains with 25 % frequency spread = coloured noise - fine as 'Rieseln', but the tone is only there at R > ~0.5, i.e. the upper half of the finger; (d) R-capped 0.85 + phase diffusion + random grain amplitude are the right anti-sterility measures.
soundBurst: Weak as specified: synchronisation needs ~1/(K - K_c) time, i.e. many cycles (at 100 Hz, 0.1-0.5 s), so K ramping 0 -> K(y) over gate*0.7 inside a 50-100 ms Puls gate never locks - every hit is a noise 'Rutsche', never a tuned grain. Invert it for bursts: start all phases coherent (R = 1, the 'Anfangsrutsch' the idea already has for vel) and let K sit below K_c so the hit is a tuned boom that crumbles into sand over the decay - that is distinctive, tempo-robust and keeps the pitch. Long Puls gates (Droehnakkorde) work as a slow lock-in only if gate >= ~0.3 s.
failureModes: Cost as written (per-sample mean field + Math.pow pulse) ~13 units; needs sub-rate coupling, tabled pulse shape or event-based impulses, and a bench measurement before build
No snap: first-order Kuramoto with N = 24 is a continuous, fluctuating crossfade; the promised 'moment of locking' needs inertia/adaptive coupling for hysteresis [A]
Synced state = buzzy pulse train above ~300 Hz; restrict/fold the range to 40-200 Hz with a body lowpass, or it is a rough Koerner
Tone only in the upper half of the finger range (R > 0.5); lower half is noise - acceptable as Rieseln, but must be shaped
Puls hits cannot lock inside short gates; use coherent start + decay (boom crumbling to sand) instead of K ramp-up
First worklet engine moves the whole graph to the worklet thread (R: webaudio.md section 2) - decide once, load at initAudio, never on first touch
Native fallback (noise <-> pulse PeriodicWave crossfade with jitter FM) is a different, lesser instrument; label 'vereinfacht' and hide the lock-in gesture there
Phase diffusion and random amplitudes must be bounded; a thrown exception in process() silences the voice for good (R: section 3)
Glühwurm (sub-audio Kuramoto) and Duene share a story; keep Duene's identity as 'the transition is the pitch', Gluehwurm's as rhythm
verdict: Rare: audio-rate Kuramoto synthesis already exists in Nolan Lem's Kuroscillators (Max), the browser Kuramoto drone, Ling's Synchronized Synthesis and - as a mainstream effect - Chiral Audio's Foxfire (16-voice Kuramoto chorus with a Coupling knob that 'flickers at the critical point'); none is a pitched instrument whose playable control is the noise-to-tone transition, so the instrument is unfound, but the mechanism is not. Worklet-only, and the quoted 0.75 units is wrong for the design as written (per-sample mean field plus a Math.pow pulse is ~13 units); with sub-rate coupling and tabled pulses it is ~1.1, event-based impulses ~0.6 - measure first. Held, it is the most original gesture of the four, but first-order Kuramoto with 24 grains gives a mushy continuous crossfade, not a 'moment of locking' (inertia or adaptive coupling for hysteresis), and the synced state is a buzzy pulse train unless the range stays 40-200 Hz. Puls hits cannot lock inside short gates; invert them (coherent start crumbling into sand) and the hit becomes distinctive.
